text:
Sam B (Solutions): FYI new deal with NovaHealth — they require private connectivity + static egress IPs and asked us to complete a security questionnaire.
Maya R (NetEng): Got it. Do they want PrivateLink or VPC peering? Both have tradeoffs.
Sam B (Solutions): Legal prefers PrivateLink because it avoids cross-account peering, but their infra team wants client IP preservation for audit logs.
Alex T: PrivateLink terminates at our ENI and the source IP will be the ENI -> we can't preserve original client src without a proxy. Can we surface X-Forwarded-For from our side? :thinking:  
Maya R (NetEng): We can add X-Forwarded-For at the application/proxy layer. Alternative is VPC peering + route tables to preserve src IP, but peering requires cross-account routing acceptance.
Rebecca (AE): Quick pricing question — how much does a 1-month POC cost if they need 2 static EIPs and private deploy? They're price sensitive.
Sam B (Solutions): Ballpark: base POC infra + per-EIP charge. I'll pull the exact numbers from pricing ops. Also need to answer security Qs around TLS termination, KMS integration, and audit logs.
Maya R (NetEng): Minimal firewall guidance for PrivateLink egress (customer side) — note these are examples, they will substitute ranges: 
```
# Customer egress ACL (example)
allow tcp any 443 to 34.120.200.0/24   # Redwood PrivateLink endpoint AZs
allow udp any 53 to 10.0.0.2         # internal DNS resolver
allow tcp any 22 to 10.0.1.5         # bastion for admin (if needed)
```
Alex T: They mentioned SD-WAN and BFD for fast failover. Recommend we document BFD + MTU guidance for the S2S tunnel. BFD is optional but improves failover times with SD-WAN controllers.
InfraBot: New network checklist created: https://redwood.internal/handbook/poc-network-checklist (access: redwood employees).
Rebecca (AE): They also asked for SOC2 report and an exportable security pack. I'll attach the standard SOC2 link, but NetEng — confirm PrivateDeploy supports customer-managed KMS/HSM.
Maya R (NetEng): For PrivateDeploy we support customer KMS integration via IAM roles for key access; HSM possible via partner integrations (we'll note this in questionnaire). We also support VPC flow logs and host-level audit logs forwarded to their S3 or SIEM.
Alex T: Security question from their team: can we provide a firewall snippet that enforces SNI allowlist for TLS-inspect environments? Example below.
```
# SNI allowlist example for perimeter firewall
ALLOW:
  - hostname: api.redwood-internal.example
    dest_port: 443
    sni: api.redwood-internal.example
```
Sam B (Solutions): Follow-ups before the call: (1) confirm whether NovaHealth can host an egress proxy in their VPC (2) confirm SLA targets for the POC (3) confirm budget for number of EIPs. I'll schedule a 30m call with their infra lead tomorrow 10am PT.
Maya R (NetEng): If they cannot run an egress proxy, propose Dedicated PrivateDeploy with static NAT EIP(s). That preserves outbound IPs for allowlists but we can't preserve original client IP; recommend app-level XFF headers for audit events.
Rebecca (AE): I'll prepare the pricing sheet: 1-month POC, 2 EIPs, optional BFD tunnel setup, and a security pack. Will include both PrivateLink and peering cost comparisons.
Sam B (Solutions): Also asking: will we expose per-route logging for PrivateLink connections? They want per-tenant request traces.
Maya R (NetEng): We can export request-level logs and correlate via request-id headers. For PrivateDeploy we can forward logs and support per-route dashboards in Redwood Console (retention depends on plan).
Alex T: Note on TLS-inspect customers: if they terminate TLS on their side, they must allow SNI for our hostname or pin certs. Document MTU and MSS clamping for tunnels to avoid fragmentation.
Sam B (Solutions): OK — action items: Maya add KMS/HSM and logging answers to the questionnaire, Alex provide BFD/MTU doc and firewall snippets, Rebecca send pricing and SOC2 artifacts. I'll run the call invite.
Rebecca (AE): tagging @Maya R (NetEng) and @Alex T for the call invite.
Maya R (NetEng): ack
Alex T: ack
Sam B (Solutions): Thanks team — noting the customer also asked for an inbound low-latency peering option later in the roadmap. We'll draft both PrivateLink-first and peering-first architectures in the handoff doc.
